Subject: GPU SKU anchoring & ops constraints for Polaris Dedicated pilot

Hi Samira / Taylor,

Following our call earlier — attaching a short profile you sent (polaris_infra_profile.pdf) and a quick SKU anchoring spreadsheet (sku_anchor_calc.xlsx) so we can align on procurement constraints. High-level asks from our side so we can lock an initial Dedicated proposal: 

- Confirm P95 latency target (in ms) and whether you want latency-first on user-facing generation endpoints.
- Peak concurrent qps (sustained windows vs marketing bursts) — you mentioned a marketing campaign spike, want the exact cadence.
- Typical and max context length (tokens) for primary workload (inference generation) and percentage of calls that read/write long KV caches.
- Any strict data residency or KMS requirements beyond standard US/EU options.

Our initial read: long-context generation with KV cache pressure pushes toward H100/A100 depending on effective model quant and optimizer. L4 looks attractive for short-context low-latency embedding/aux calls. But we need the numbers above before we recommend a reserve/burst mix.

Ops note: we have a standard runoff for reserve commits — 4-8 week lead time for A100/H100 racks in most regions, L4 often available faster as burst. Also include Priyom on bench/tiling constraints.

Thanks — planning to draft a proposal this week if we have those numbers.

Best,
Olga
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Olga — thanks, attaching a short answers doc inline below.

- P95 target: 220ms for customer-facing generation (we can tolerate occasional spikes to 350ms if cost savings are material).
- Baseline sustained qps: 25 qps during business hours (US-east peak), bursts: up to 150 qps for ~3 hours during campaign days (~6x).
- Context: typical 512 tokens, heavy flows to 8k tokens for analytics users (approx 12% of calls), rare 32k sessions for enterprise reports (1% of calls).
- KV/cache: ~30% of calls rely on warm KV cache; cold starts increase token compute by ~15%.
- Data residency: must keep logs in US region only, KMS integration required (customer-managed KMS).

Budget: Polaris has a target committed spend for Dedicated that caps monthly reserved GPU spend; we can flex up to 20% on burst consumption but need clarity on unit economics per GPU type.

Happy to discuss tradeoffs tomorrow.

—Samira
Director, Infrastructure
Polaris AI

Subject: Re: GPU SKU anchoring & ops constraints for Polaris Dedicated pilot

Samira — thanks for the specifics, that helps a lot. FWIW, my recommendation based on those profiles:

- Anchor compute around A100 for the reserved pool. Rationale: A100 provides a balanced memory footprint for 8k sessions with good throughput and is typically the best cost/latency compromise versus H100 at reserve price.
- Reserve baseline: 8 x A100 (dense) to cover sustained 25 qps and staggered long-context work with KV caching.
- Burst pool: 4 x L4 for low-latency short-context traffic and up to 4 x H100 as optional burst for heavy 32k report windows (H100 only when required due to higher reserved costs).
- Fallback rules: route to A100 first for long contexts, L4 for short contexts. H100 reserved only when you commit to latency-first SLAs for enterprise report workloads.

Operational ask: confirm whether Polaris can commit to a 12-month reserve window for the A100s. That commitment materially lowers the unit cost and keeps overall blended cost near your target. If you prefer shorter terms, we can rebalance with more L4 burst but expect higher per-token cost on long-context paths.

I can put numbers into the spreadsheet Olga attached and produce a blended tokens-per-dollar estimate.

Cheers,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: GPU SKU anchoring & ops constraints for Polaris Dedicated pilot

Ben / Olga / Samira — technical ops perspective with some numbers and an ops runbook stub attached. Key points: 

- Memory headroom: for the 8k token modality, A100 80GB (v2) typically requires ~58GB usable after model parameters and KV cache in fp16; H100 gives ~20% extra headroom but at ~1.4x cost for reserve. Using int8 quantization on the generation model can lower memory by ~25-30% with modest quality checks.
- Tiling & slotting: with our continuous batching runtime, we can pack smaller short-context requests on L4 with minimal latency overhead. Long sessions should be pinned to A100/H100 nodes to avoid eviction churn.
- Fallback logic (ops):
  - Normal: route gen->A100, emb->L4.
  - On A100 saturation: opportunistic spill to H100 if available (higher cost), otherwise apply soft degradation by reducing max_output_tokens for non-critical flows.
  - Cold KV warms: use a background pre-warm pipeline during campaign ramp windows to reduce cold-start spikes.
- Procurement/lead time: A100 reserve fulfillment estimate is 6-10 weeks; H100 has longer lead times depending on region and vendor stock. L4 burst is the quickest to spin up; good candidate for immediate burst coverage.

I'll attach the ops runbook excerpt (ops_tiling_runbook.md) with example routing policies and a sample canary for rollout. If Polaris wants to minimize cost while preserving most long-context quality, recommend: 8 x A100 reserved + 4 x L4 burst + optional 2-4 H100 on a short-term burst or premium SLA.

Priyom
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
